paper.title_en: Quantitative Junction Transport Modeling of RHIC Charge and Baryon Stopping
paper.abstract_en: Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.
